title: About ₹0.80 estimated cost per researched lead
outcome: A lead research pipeline that replaced manual research.
context: Vastav Intellect works in a specialised space where understanding a prospect matters as much as finding one. Two employees researched every incoming lead by hand, about ₹40,000 a month in staffing, and the work grew with every new lead.
problem: The founder wanted to hand over a spreadsheet of leads and get back a short brief on each prospect and what to offer them. A general-purpose AI tool could do it for a few leads, but at hundreds or thousands it became too expensive.
built: We costed the options first, then split lead research into three stages, each handled by the cheapest tool that does the job well, run by two workers on a Django and MongoDB backend.

components.name: Discover: Serper
components.detail: Web search as its own stage, not bundled into an all-in-one AI research call.

components.name: Extract: Jina AI
components.detail: Turns the pages found into usable material for analysis.

components.name: Interpret: Gemini
components.detail: A lighter model classifies findings and spots opportunities without paying for premium reasoning on every step.

components.name: Two-worker execution
components.detail: Research and processing run without blocking each other.

flow: Classify and brief the sales team
result: Estimated research cost fell to about ₹0.80 per lead, from about ₹2–₹3 with a web-search agent (roughly 60–73% less) and ₹5–₹8 with general-purpose AI research (up to about 90% less).
resultDefinition: Our own estimates for this workflow, not independently audited. Actual cost depends on research depth, retries and usage.
